purpose: Pitolisant is used to help people with narcolepsy stay awake during the day and reduce sudden muscle weakness (called cataplexy) triggered by emotions. It is approved for adults who have narcolepsy, a sleep disorder that causes extreme daytime sleepiness. It can help you feel more alert and function better during your daily activities.
how_it_works: Your brain has a chemical called histamine that helps keep you awake and alert. Pitolisant works by blocking certain receptors in the brain that normally slow down histamine production. By blocking those receptors, it tells your brain to make more histamine, which helps boost wakefulness and alertness naturally.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, trouble sleeping (insomnia), nausea, feeling anxious or irritable, dizziness, and an upset stomach. Some people may also notice upper respiratory symptoms like a runny nose. Most side effects are mild and may improve as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as pitolisant may not be safe in these situations. It can also affect the heart rhythm (QT prolongation), so let your doctor know if you have any heart conditions or take other medications that affect your heart. Avoid taking it with certain medications that interact with it, including some antidepressants and antipsychotics. It may also make hormonal birth control less effective, so use a backup method of contraception.
typical_dosing: Pitolisant is taken once a day by mouth in the morning. You usually start at a low dose of 8.9 mg per day for the first week. Your doctor may increase the dose to 17.8 mg per day and then up to the maximum dose of 35.6 mg per day depending on how well it works for you and how you tolerate it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
